subject: Demotion clause & bucket substitution — pricing redline (Exhibit D)
messages:
From: Nate Chen <nate.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed redline: demotion/pack substitution language (Exhibit D)

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we talked about on the demo, Nimbus needs more flexibility to shift volume between premium and standard packs as utilization patterns change across clinics. Attached is our proposed redline to Exhibit D that introduces: 1) a "demotion" mechanism to move committed units from premium SKUs to standard SKUs up to a defined percentage per quarter; and 2) a bucket-substitution rule to allow reassigning unused units within the same product family.

High-level asks from us:
- Demotion up to 20% per quarter, cumulative, with no retroactive true-up.
- Ability to substitute across bundles within a 90-day window without financial penalty.

We intentionally kept the language broad to simplify ops, but can tighten if you need guardrails. Please review with pricing/legal and let us know constraints you need. Our legal team (legal@nimbushealth.com) is cc'd with a clean redline attached (Nimbus_ExhibitD_proposed_redline.pdf).

Would like to resolve final language before the SOW signature next week.

Thanks,
Nate Chen
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
Attachment: Nimbus_ExhibitD_proposed_redline.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redline: demotion/pack substitution language (Exhibit D)

Team — looping you in. Nimbus is asking for fairly open demotion/substitution terms in Exhibit D. My quick concerns: potential revenue leakage if we allow 20% demotion with no true-up, and operational friction if substitutions are unconstrained (affects capacity planning and pack inventory).

Karthik — can you estimate the monthly throughput/slot impact if up to 20% of committed premium units migrate to standard? Are there quant thresholds where this materially changes pricing bands?

Laura — from legal: would a capped demotion with a rolling true-up (e.g., allow 10% per quarter with annual true-up) be acceptable? Or should we do a clawback mechanism tied to realized usage?

Marissa — any commercial precedent you recommend (customer-side concessions vs. revenue protection constructs)? If possible, can you produce a short marked-up language we can send back today? We need a proposal that is legal-ready before Tuesday.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nate Chen <nate.chen@nimbushealth.com>, legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 13:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redline: demotion/pack substitution language (Exhibit D)

Marcus / all — quick draft comments attached (Marissa_redline_comments.docx). Summary of the commercial position I recommend:

- Accept a limited demotion window but tighten to 10% per quarter (non-cumulative) with a one-time annual reconciliation (true-up) to the higher-priced SKU. This protects our unit economics while giving Nimbus breathing room.
- Allow substitutions within product families inside a 60-day window post-invoice but only up to 15% of the billed units per month. Any substitutions beyond that would trigger an adjustment at standard rates.
- Add an operational notice requirement: customer must provide substitution notice 14 days prior to the intended shift so our ops team can reallocate capacity.

I flagged specific clauses in the attached doc. If legal and Karthik sign off, I can send the marked-up language as a tracked-change PDF to Nate and his counsel.

Attachment: Marissa_redline_comments.docx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: legal@nimbushealth.com <legal@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nate Chen <nate.chen@nimbushealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@nimbushealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 16:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redline: demotion/pack substitution language (Exhibit D)

Marissa / Marcus — thanks for the quick review and the narrower proposals. Nimbus legal is generally supportive of a constrained approach but asks two changes for commercial acceptance:

1) Remove the annual true-up requiring Nimbus to pay the higher SKU retroactively; instead, allow a situational clawback where we reconcile only if the cumulative demotion in a 12-month period exceeds 25%.
2) Expand the substitution window to 90 days (from 60) but retain the 14-day operational notice; Nimbus says 60 days is tight for procurement cycles across sites.

If Redwood can agree to those two adjustments, we can sign Exhibit D with the revised limits. Attached is a short note from our counsel.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Counsel, Nimbus Health
Attachment: Nimbus_legal_note.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Nate Chen <nate.chen@nimbushealth.com>, legal@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redline: demotion/pack substitution language (Exhibit D)

Samir / Nate — appreciate the swift feedback and the flexibility. Proposed final position from Redwood (to close before SOW signature):

- Demotion: allow up to 10% per quarter (non-cumulative) with a mandatory flagging of cumulative demotions. If cumulative demotion in any rolling 12-month window exceeds 25%, a clawback equal to the weighted-price difference will be applied for the excess.
- Substitution: allow substitutions within product families up to 15% of billed units per month, within a 90-day window; 14-day operational notice required. Substitutions beyond 15% per month are billed at standard rates.

Marissa and Laura will prepare the final tracked-change Exhibit D incorporating the clawback mechanics and an ops-notice clause. Karthik: we'll need an internal ops note outlining how substitution notices will be processed; I'll create a short summary file and share with Nimbus.

If that sounds acceptable, we'll send the final Exhibit D and aim to get countersigned tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
